ko.title: [국제 물류 #13] 단 한 척의 배, 6일간의 마비, 수십억 달러의 손실: 공급망 리스크의 실체

segments.src: > Global supply chains are built for efficiency, but a single blocked canal or jammed port can ripple across the world. Resilience is about planning for the day things go wrong.
segments.tr: > 글로벌 공급망은 효율성을 위해 구축되었지만, 운하가 하나만 막히거나 항구가 정체되어도 전 세계로 그 여파가 퍼질 수 있습니다. 회복탄력성이란 문제가 발생할 상황을 미리 대비하는 것입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: **글로벌 공급망(global supply chain)**은 원자재를 선반 위의 제품으로 바꾸는 네트워크입니다.

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: 스마트폰 하나를 예로 들면, 아프리카에서 채굴된 광물, 대만에서 만든 칩, 중국에서 조립된 부품이 오하이오주의 매장으로 배송되는 과정을 거칩니다.

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: 물류는 이 모든 것을 물리적으로 이동시키는 부분으로, 선박, 트럭, 기차, 비행기, 창고, 항구가 포함됩니다.

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: 수십 년 동안 기업들은 이러한 네트워크를 **저비용 및 속도**에 맞춰 최적화했습니다.

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: 널리 쓰이는 접근 방식은 **적시 생산 방식(just-in-time, JIT)**입니다. 재고를 최대한 적게 보유하고 필요한 시점에 부품이 도착하도록 하는 것입니다.

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: JIT는 창고 비용과 재고 부담을 줄여주지만, 여유 공간이 거의 없습니다.

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: 연결 고리 하나가 끊어지면 완충 장치가 전혀 없는 셈입니다.

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: 물류 리스크는 무역의 상당 부분이 통과해야 하는 좁은 통로인 **병목 지점(chokepoints)**에 집중되는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: 잘 알려진 세 가지 사례는 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **수에즈 운하:** 유럽과 아시아를 연결하며 전 세계 무역량의 약 12%를 담당합니다.

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **파나마 운하:** 대서양과 태평양을 연결하며, 아시아에서 미국 동부 해안으로 들어오는 수입품에 매우 중요합니다.

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **말라카 해협:** 인도양과 태평양 사이의 혼잡한 항로입니다.

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: 최근 몇 년간 우리는 몇 가지 뼈아픈 교훈을 얻었습니다.

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **2021년 3월, 에버 기븐(Ever Given)호:** 400미터 길이의 컨테이너선이 좌초되어 6일 동안 수에즈 운하를 막았습니다. 양쪽 끝에 수백 척의 배가 줄을 섰고, 분석가들은 운하가 막힌 매일 약 90억~100억 달러 규모의 상품이 발이 묶인 것으로 추산했습니다.

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021~2022년, 항구 적체:** 팬데믹 시대의 수요 폭증으로 항구가 마비되었고, 중국에서 미국 서부 해안으로 가는 컨테이너 운송료가 40피트 컨테이너당 2,000달러 미만에서 최고 약 20,000달러까지 치솟았습니다.

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023년, 파나마 가뭄:** 운하의 갑문을 채우는 호수의 수위가 낮아지면서 당국은 일일 통과 선박 수와 선박의 적재량을 제한해야 했습니다.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **2023년 말 이후, 홍해:** 상선에 대한 공격으로 인해 많은 선사가 수에즈 운하를 피해 아프리카 희망봉을 돌아가는 항로를 택했습니다. 이 우회 경로는 보통 10~14일의 시간과 막대한 연료가 추가로 소요됩니다.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: 이 모든 문제에 대한 해답은 **회복탄력성(resilience)**입니다. 이는 공급망이 충격을 흡수하고 빠르게 회복하는 능력을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: 일반적인 전략은 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **다변화:** 하나 이상의 공급업체, 항구 또는 경로를 사용하는 것(종종 이중 또는 다중 소싱이라고 함).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **완충 장치:** 약간의 **안전 재고(safety stock)**를 유지하는 것. 이는 "적시 생산(just-in-time)"에서 "만약의 사태 대비(just-in-case)"로의 전환입니다.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **니어쇼어링 또는 프렌드쇼어링:** 생산 시설을 본국 근처나 우방국으로 이전하는 것.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **가시성:** 배송 및 공급업체 리스크를 실시간으로 추적하여 문제를 조기에 파악하는 것.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: 이러한 전략의 장단점은 말하기는 쉽지만 관리하기는 어렵습니다. 회복탄력성을 갖추려면 비용이 듭니다.

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: 기업은 어느 정도의 보험료를 지불할 의향이 있는지 결정해야 합니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속의 물류

segments.src: Think back to fall 2021.
segments.tr: 2021년 가을을 떠올려 보세요.

segments.src: Off the coast of Southern California, dozens of container ships sat anchored and waited, sometimes for weeks, to unload at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.
segments.tr: 남부 캘리포니아 해안에는 수십 척의 컨테이너선이 닻을 내리고 로스앤젤레스항과 롱비치항에서 하역하기 위해 몇 주씩 대기했습니다.

segments.src: Together those two ports handle a large share of U.S.
segments.tr: 이 두 항구는 미국으로 들어오는 아시아발

segments.src: imports from Asia.
segments.tr: 수입품의 상당 부분을 처리합니다.

segments.src: Early in 2022 the queue went past 100 ships.
segments.tr: 2022년 초에는 대기 중인 선박이 100척을 넘어섰습니다.

segments.src: People felt it at home.
segments.tr: 사람들은 가정에서 이를 체감했습니다.

segments.src: Retailers warned customers to start holiday shopping early.
segments.tr: 소매업체들은 고객들에게 연말 쇼핑을 서두르라고 경고했습니다.

segments.src: Furniture orders that once took a few weeks took months.
segments.tr: 몇 주면 오던 가구 주문이 몇 달씩 걸리기도 했습니다.

segments.src: Some big retailers chartered their own ships to get goods in.
segments.tr: 일부 대형 소매업체는 물건을 받기 위해 직접 선박을 전세 내기도 했습니다.

segments.src: The higher shipping costs fed into store prices and helped push up U.S.
segments.tr: 상승한 운송 비용은 매장 가격에 반영되어 미국

segments.src: inflation.
segments.tr: 인플레이션을 부추기는 요인이 되었습니다.

segments.src: No single thing caused it.
segments.tr: 단 하나의 원인 때문이 아니었습니다.

segments.src: Online orders surged, warehouses were short on workers, there weren't enough truck drivers or chassis (the trailers containers sit on), and empty containers were stuck in the wrong places.
segments.tr: 온라인 주문 급증, 창고 인력 부족, 트럭 운전사나 섀시(컨테이너를 싣는 트레일러) 부족, 빈 컨테이너가 엉뚱한 곳에 방치되는 등 여러 문제가 겹쳤습니다.

segments.src: Each small bottleneck made the others worse.
segments.tr: 작은 병목 현상 하나하나가 다른 문제들을 악화시켰습니다.

segments.src: That is the core lesson of supply chain risk: **systems built with no slack can turn small problems into big ones.**
segments.tr: 이것이 바로 공급망 리스크의 핵심 교훈입니다. **여유 없이 구축된 시스템은 작은 문제를 큰 문제로 키울 수 있습니다.**

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Global supply chains are tuned for efficiency, so they often have little slack and depend on a few chokepoints like the Suez and Panama Canals.
segments.tr: 1. 글로벌 공급망은 효율성에 맞춰져 있어 여유가 거의 없고, 수에즈 운하나 파나마 운하와 같은 몇몇 병목 지점에 의존합니다.

segments.src: 2. Events like the Ever Given grounding, the 2021 port backlogs, the Panama drought, and the Red Sea diversions show how one disruption spreads worldwide.
segments.tr: 2. 에버 기븐호 좌초, 2021년 항구 적체, 파나마 가뭄, 홍해 우회 사태 등은 하나의 차질이 어떻게 전 세계로 퍼지는지 보여줍니다.

segments.src: 3. Resilience strategies such as diversification, safety stock, nearshoring, and visibility lower risk, but they cost money.
segments.tr: 3. 다변화, 안전 재고, 니어쇼어링, 가시성 확보와 같은 회복탄력성 전략은 리스크를 낮추지만 비용이 발생합니다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Key Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 주요 용어

segments.src: - **Supply chain:** The full network of suppliers, manufacturers, carriers, and sellers that gets a product from raw material to customer.
segments.tr: - **공급망(Supply chain):** 원자재부터 고객에게 제품이 전달되기까지의 공급업체, 제조업체, 운송업체, 판매업체로 이루어진 전체 네트워크.

segments.src: - **Chokepoint:** A narrow route, such as a canal or strait, that a large share of trade must pass through.
segments.tr: - **병목 지점(Chokepoint):** 무역의 상당 부분이 통과해야 하는 운하나 해협과 같은 좁은 경로.

segments.src: - **Just-in-time (JIT):** An inventory approach where materials arrive only as they are needed, which keeps costs low but leaves little buffer.
segments.tr: - **적시 생산 방식(Just-in-time, JIT):** 자재가 필요한 시점에만 도착하도록 하는 재고 관리 방식으로, 비용은 낮게 유지하지만 완충 장치가 거의 없음.

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held to protect against delays or unexpected demand.
segments.tr: - **안전 재고(Safety stock):** 지연이나 예상치 못한 수요에 대비해 보유하는 추가 재고.

segments.src: - **Resilience:** A supply chain's ability to withstand a disruption and recover quickly.
segments.tr: - **회복탄력성(Resilience):** 공급망이 중단 사태를 견뎌내고 빠르게 회복하는 능력.

zh.title: [国际物流 #13] 一艘船，六天，数十亿货物滞留：供应链风险的真实面貌

segments.tr: > 全球供应链旨在追求效率，但单一运河的堵塞或港口的拥堵可能会波及全球。韧性在于为可能出错的那一天做好规划。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: **全球供应链**是将原材料转化为货架上产品的网络。

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: 一部智能手机可能使用在非洲开采的矿物、在台湾制造的芯片，并在中国完成组装，然后才运往俄亥俄州的商店。

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: 物流是物理移动所有这些物品的部分：船舶、卡车、火车、飞机、仓库和港口。

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: 几十年来，企业一直致力于将这些网络调整为**低成本和高速度**。

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: 一种流行的方法是**准时制（JIT）**库存：尽可能少地持有库存，并在需要时让零件及时到达。

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: JIT 节省了仓库和未售出商品的成本，但几乎没有缓冲空间。

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: 当一个环节断裂时，就没有缓冲余地。

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: 物流风险往往集中在**瓶颈（chokepoints）**，即大量贸易必须通过的狭窄通道。

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: 三个众所周知的例子：

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **苏伊士运河**连接欧洲和亚洲，承担了全球约 12% 的贸易量。

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **巴拿马运河**连接大西洋和太平洋，对于美国东海岸从亚洲进口货物至关重要。

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **马六甲海峡**是印度洋和太平洋之间繁忙的航道。

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: 近年来给我们上了几堂沉重的一课：

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **2021年3月，长赐号（Ever Given）：** 一艘 400 米长的集装箱船搁浅，堵塞苏伊士运河长达六天。数百艘船只在两端排队，分析师估计，堵塞期间每天约有 90 亿至 100 亿美元的货物被滞留。

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022年，港口拥堵：** 疫情期间的需求淹没了港口，从中国到美国西海岸的集装箱运费在高峰期从不到 2,000 美元飙升至每个 40 英尺集装箱约 20,000 美元。

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023年，巴拿马干旱：** 为运河船闸供水的湖泊水位下降，迫使当局限制每日通行数量以及船舶的载重。

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **2023年底至今，红海局势：** 对商船的袭击导致许多承运人避开苏伊士运河，转而绕行非洲好望角。这种绕道通常会增加 10 到 14 天的航程，并消耗大量燃料。

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: 解决所有这些问题的答案是**韧性（resilience）**：供应链吸收冲击并快速恢复的能力。

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: 常见的策略包括：

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **多元化：** 使用不止一个供应商、港口或路线（通常称为双重或多重采购）。

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **缓冲：** 保留一些**安全库存**，这是从“准时制”向“以防万一（just-in-case）”的转变。

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **近岸外包或友岸外包：** 将部分生产转移到离家更近或盟国。

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **可见性：** 实时跟踪货物和供应商风险，以便尽早发现问题。

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: 这种权衡说起来简单，但管理起来很难：韧性需要成本。

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: 企业必须决定愿意为多少保险买单。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的体现

segments.src: Think back to fall 2021.
segments.tr: 回想一下 2021 年秋天。

segments.src: Off the coast of Southern California, dozens of container ships sat anchored and waited, sometimes for weeks, to unload at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.
segments.tr: 在南加州海岸外，数十艘集装箱船抛锚等待，有时长达数周，以便在洛杉矶港和长滩港卸货。

segments.src: Together those two ports handle a large share of U.S.
segments.tr: 这两个港口合计处理了美国很大一部分

segments.src: imports from Asia.
segments.tr: 来自亚洲的进口货物。

segments.src: Early in 2022 the queue went past 100 ships.
segments.tr: 2022 年初，排队的船只超过了 100 艘。

segments.src: People felt it at home.
segments.tr: 人们在家里感受到了影响。

segments.src: Retailers warned customers to start holiday shopping early.
segments.tr: 零售商警告顾客尽早开始假日购物。

segments.src: Furniture orders that once took a few weeks took months.
segments.tr: 曾经只需几周的家具订单现在需要几个月。

segments.src: Some big retailers chartered their own ships to get goods in.
segments.tr: 一些大型零售商包租了自己的船只来运送货物。

segments.src: The higher shipping costs fed into store prices and helped push up U.S.
segments.tr: 更高的运输成本推高了商店价格，并助推了美国的

segments.src: inflation.
segments.tr: 通货膨胀。

segments.src: No single thing caused it.
segments.tr: 没有单一的原因导致这种情况。

segments.src: Online orders surged, warehouses were short on workers, there weren't enough truck drivers or chassis (the trailers containers sit on), and empty containers were stuck in the wrong places.
segments.tr: 在线订单激增，仓库工人短缺，卡车司机或底盘（集装箱放置的拖车）不足，空集装箱被困在错误的地方。

segments.src: Each small bottleneck made the others worse.
segments.tr: 每一个小的瓶颈都让其他问题变得更糟。

segments.src: That is the core lesson of supply chain risk: **systems built with no slack can turn small problems into big ones.**
segments.tr: 这就是供应链风险的核心教训：**没有缓冲的系统可以将小问题变成大问题。**

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行总结

segments.src: 1. Global supply chains are tuned for efficiency, so they often have little slack and depend on a few chokepoints like the Suez and Panama Canals.
segments.tr: 1. 全球供应链旨在追求效率，因此往往缺乏缓冲，并依赖于苏伊士运河和巴拿马运河等少数瓶颈。

segments.src: 2. Events like the Ever Given grounding, the 2021 port backlogs, the Panama drought, and the Red Sea diversions show how one disruption spreads worldwide.
segments.tr: 2. 长赐号搁浅、2021年港口积压、巴拿马干旱和红海改道等事件表明，单一的中断是如何在全球范围内蔓延的。

segments.src: 3. Resilience strategies such as diversification, safety stock, nearshoring, and visibility lower risk, but they cost money.
segments.tr: 3. 多元化、安全库存、近岸外包和可见性等韧性策略可以降低风险，但它们需要成本。

segments.src: ## 📚 Key Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 关键术语

segments.src: - **Supply chain:** The full network of suppliers, manufacturers, carriers, and sellers that gets a product from raw material to customer.
segments.tr: - **供应链（Supply chain）：** 将产品从原材料到客户手中的完整供应商、制造商、承运人和销售商网络。

segments.src: - **Chokepoint:** A narrow route, such as a canal or strait, that a large share of trade must pass through.
segments.tr: - **瓶颈（Chokepoint）：** 大量贸易必须通过的狭窄路线，如运河或海峡。

segments.src: - **Just-in-time (JIT):** An inventory approach where materials arrive only as they are needed, which keeps costs low but leaves little buffer.
segments.tr: - **准时制（Just-in-time, JIT）：** 一种库存方法，材料仅在需要时才到达，这保持了低成本但几乎没有缓冲。

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held to protect against delays or unexpected demand.
segments.tr: - **安全库存（Safety stock）：** 为防止延误或意外需求而持有的额外库存。

segments.src: - **Resilience:** A supply chain's ability to withstand a disruption and recover quickly.
segments.tr: - **韧性（Resilience）：** 供应链抵御中断并快速恢复的能力。

hi.title: [International Logistics #13] One Ship, Six Days, Billions Stuck: What Supply Chain Risk Really Looks Like

segments.src: > Global supply chains are built for efficiency, but a single blocked canal or jammed port can ripple across the world. Resilience is about planning for the day things go wrong.
segments.tr: > वैश्विक आपूर्ति श्रृंखलाएं दक्षता के लिए बनाई गई हैं, लेकिन एक अवरुद्ध नहर या जाम बंदरगाह दुनिया भर में हलचल पैदा कर सकता है। लचीलापन (Resilience) का अर्थ है उस दिन के लिए योजना बनाना जब चीजें गलत हो जाती हैं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: एक **वैश्विक आपूर्ति श्रृंखला (global supply chain)** वह नेटवर्क है जो कच्चे माल को आपके शेल्फ पर मौजूद उत्पादों में बदल देता है।

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: एक स्मार्टफोन में अफ्रीका में खनन किए गए खनिज, ताइवान में बने चिप्स और चीन में किया गया असेंबली कार्य शामिल हो सकता है, इससे पहले कि वह ओहियो के किसी स्टोर में भेजा जाए।

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: लॉजिस्टिक्स वह हिस्सा है जो भौतिक रूप से इन सभी को स्थानांतरित करता है: जहाज, ट्रक, ट्रेन, विमान, गोदाम और बंदरगाह।

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: दशकों से, कंपनियों ने इन नेटवर्कों को **कम लागत और गति** के लिए ट्यून किया है।

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: एक लोकप्रिय दृष्टिकोण **जस्ट-इन-टाइम (JIT)** इन्वेंट्री है: जितना संभव हो उतना कम स्टॉक रखें और पुर्जे ठीक उसी समय मंगवाएं जब आपको उनकी आवश्यकता हो।

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: JIT गोदामों और बिना बिके माल पर पैसे बचाता है, लेकिन इसमें बहुत कम गुंजाइश (slack) बचती है।

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: जब एक कड़ी टूटती है, तो कोई कुशन नहीं होता है।

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: लॉजिस्टिक्स में जोखिम **चोकपॉइंट्स (chokepoints)** पर इकट्ठा होता है, जो ऐसे संकीर्ण मार्ग हैं जिनसे व्यापार का एक बड़ा हिस्सा गुजरता है।

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: तीन प्रसिद्ध उदाहरण:

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **स्वेज नहर (The Suez Canal)** यूरोप और एशिया को जोड़ती है और विश्व व्यापार का लगभग 12% हिस्सा ले जाती है।

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **पनामा नहर (The Panama Canal)** अटलांटिक और प्रशांत को जोड़ती है और एशिया से अमेरिकी पूर्वी तट के आयात के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **मलक्का जलडमरूमध्य (The Strait of Malacca)** हिंद महासागर और प्रशांत के बीच एक भीड़भाड़ वाला मार्ग है।

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: हाल के वर्षों ने हमें कई कठिन सबक दिए हैं:

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **मार्च 2021, एवर गिवेन (Ever Given):** 400 मीटर लंबा एक कंटेनर जहाज जमीन पर फंस गया और छह दिनों तक स्वेज नहर को अवरुद्ध कर दिया। दोनों सिरों पर सैकड़ों जहाज कतार में खड़े थे, और विश्लेषकों का अनुमान है कि रुकावट के प्रत्येक दिन के लिए लगभग $9–10 बिलियन का माल फंसा हुआ था।

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022, बंदरगाह की भीड़:** महामारी के दौर की मांग ने बंदरगाहों को भर दिया, और चीन से अमेरिकी पश्चिमी तट तक कंटेनर शिपिंग दरें चरम पर 40-फुट कंटेनर के लिए $2,000 से कम से बढ़कर लगभग $20,000 हो गईं।

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023, पनामा सूखा:** नहर के लॉक को भरने वाली झील में पानी का स्तर कम होने के कारण अधिकारियों को दैनिक पारगमन और जहाजों के भार को सीमित करने के लिए मजबूर होना पड़ा।

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **2023 के अंत से आगे, लाल सागर:** व्यापारी जहाजों पर हमलों के कारण कई वाहकों ने स्वेज से बचने और इसके बजाय अफ्रीका के केप ऑफ गुड होप के चारों ओर यात्रा करने का निर्णय लिया। वह चक्कर आमतौर पर 10 से 14 दिन और बहुत सारा ईंधन जोड़ता है।

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: इन सबका उत्तर **लचीलापन (resilience)** है: झटके को सोखने और जल्दी से उबरने की आपूर्ति श्रृंखला की क्षमता।

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: सामान्य रणनीतियों में शामिल हैं:

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **विविधीकरण (Diversification):** एक से अधिक आपूर्तिकर्ता, बंदरगाह या मार्ग का उपयोग करना (जिसे अक्सर डुअल या मल्टी-सोर्सिंग कहा जाता है)।

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **बफ़र्स (Buffers):** कुछ **सुरक्षा स्टॉक (safety stock)** रखना, जो "जस्ट-इन-टाइम" से "जस्ट-इन-केस" की ओर एक बदलाव है।

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **नियरशोरिंग या फ्रेंडशोरिंग:** कुछ उत्पादन को घर के करीब या मित्र देशों में ले जाना।

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **दृश्यता (Visibility):** वास्तविक समय में शिपमेंट और आपूर्तिकर्ता जोखिमों को ट्रैक करना ताकि समस्याएं जल्दी दिखाई दें।

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: ट्रेड-ऑफ को बताना आसान है और प्रबंधित करना कठिन: लचीलेपन में पैसा खर्च होता है।

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: एक व्यवसाय को यह तय करना होता है कि वह कितनी बीमा राशि का भुगतान करने को तैयार है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## दैनिक जीवन में

segments.src: Think back to fall 2021.

es.title: [Logística Internacional #13] Un barco, seis días, miles de millones bloqueados: cómo es realmente el riesgo en la cadena de suministro

segments.src: > Global supply chains are built for efficiency, but a single blocked canal or jammed port can ripple across the world. Resilience is about planning for the day things go wrong.
segments.tr: > Las cadenas de suministro globales están diseñadas para la eficiencia, pero un solo canal bloqueado o un puerto congestionado pueden tener repercusiones en todo el mundo. La resiliencia consiste en planificar para el día en que las cosas salen mal.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: Una **cadena de suministro global** es la red que convierte las materias primas en los productos que están en su estantería.

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: Un teléfono inteligente puede utilizar minerales extraídos en África, chips fabricados en Taiwán y ensamblaje realizado en China antes de enviarse a una tienda en Ohio.

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: La logística es la parte que mueve físicamente todo esto: barcos, camiones, trenes, aviones, almacenes y puertos.

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: Durante décadas, las empresas ajustaron estas redes para lograr **bajo costo y velocidad**.

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: Un enfoque popular es el **justo a tiempo (JIT)**: mantener la menor cantidad de existencias posible y hacer que las piezas lleguen justo cuando las necesitas.

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: El JIT ahorra dinero en almacenes y productos no vendidos, pero deja muy poco margen de maniobra.

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: Cuando un eslabón se rompe, no hay amortiguación.

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: El riesgo en la logística tiende a acumularse en los **puntos de estrangulamiento**, pasos estrechos por los que debe pasar una gran parte del comercio.

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: Tres ejemplos bien conocidos:

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **El Canal de Suez** conecta Europa y Asia y transporta aproximadamente el 12% del comercio mundial.

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **El Canal de Panamá** conecta el Atlántico y el Pacífico y es vital para las importaciones de la costa este de EE. UU. desde Asia.

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **El Estrecho de Malaca** es un carril muy transitado entre el Océano Índico y el Pacífico.

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: Los últimos años nos dieron varias lecciones difíciles:

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **Marzo de 2021, el Ever Given:** Un buque portacontenedores de 400 metros encalló y bloqueó el Canal de Suez durante seis días. Cientos de barcos hicieron cola en ambos extremos, y los analistas estimaron que alrededor de $9–10 mil millones en mercancías quedaron retenidos por cada día de bloqueo.

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022, congestión portuaria:** La demanda de la era de la pandemia inundó los puertos, y las tarifas de envío de contenedores desde China a la costa oeste de EE. UU. saltaron de menos de $2,000 a aproximadamente $20,000 por contenedor de 40 pies en el pico.

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023, sequía en Panamá:** Los bajos niveles de agua en el lago que alimenta las esclusas del canal obligaron a las autoridades a limitar los tránsitos diarios y la carga máxima de los barcos.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **Finales de 2023 en adelante, el Mar Rojo:** Los ataques a buques mercantes llevaron a muchos transportistas a evitar Suez y navegar alrededor del Cabo de Buena Esperanza en África. Ese desvío suele añadir de 10 a 14 días y mucho combustible.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: La respuesta a todo esto es la **resiliencia**: la capacidad de una cadena de suministro para absorber un impacto y recuperarse rápidamente.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: Las estrategias comunes incluyen:

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **Diversificación:** utilizar más de un proveedor, puerto o ruta (a menudo llamado abastecimiento dual o múltiple).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **Amortiguadores:** mantener algo de **stock de seguridad**, lo cual es un cambio del "justo a tiempo" hacia el "por si acaso".

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring o friendshoring:** trasladar parte de la producción más cerca de casa o a países aliados.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **Visibilidad:** rastrear los envíos y los riesgos de los proveedores en tiempo real para que los problemas aparezcan temprano.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: La compensación es simple de expresar y difícil de gestionar: la resiliencia cuesta dinero.

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: Una empresa tiene que decidir cuánto seguro está dispuesta a pagar.

ar.title: [الخدمات اللوجستية الدولية #13] سفينة واحدة، ستة أيام، مليارات عالقة: كيف تبدو مخاطر سلاسل التوريد حقاً

segments.src: > Global supply chains are built for efficiency, but a single blocked canal or jammed port can ripple across the world. Resilience is about planning for the day things go wrong.
segments.tr: > تم بناء سلاسل التوريد العالمية لتحقيق الكفاءة، ولكن قناة واحدة مسدودة أو ميناء مزدحم يمكن أن يسبب اضطرابات في جميع أنحاء العالم. المرونة تتعلق بالتخطيط لليوم الذي تسوء فيه الأمور.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: سلسلة التوريد العالمية هي الشبكة التي تحول المواد الخام إلى المنتجات الموجودة على رفوفك.

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: قد يستخدم الهاتف الذكي معادن مستخرجة من أفريقيا، ورقائق مصنوعة في تايوان، ويتم تجميعه في الصين قبل شحنه إلى متجر في أوهايو.

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: الخدمات اللوجستية هي الجزء الذي ينقل كل هذا مادياً: السفن، والشاحنات، والقطارات، والطائرات، والمستودعات، والموانئ.

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: لعقود من الزمن، قامت الشركات بضبط هذه الشبكات لتحقيق **تكلفة منخفضة وسرعة**.

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: نهج شائع هو مخزون **التسليم في الوقت المحدد (JIT)**: الاحتفاظ بأقل قدر ممكن من المخزون ووصول الأجزاء في الوقت الذي تحتاجها فيه بالضبط.

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: يوفر نظام JIT المال في المستودعات والسلع غير المباعة، لكنه لا يترك مجالاً كبيراً للمناورة.

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: عندما تنكسر حلقة واحدة، لا توجد وسادة أمان.

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: تميل المخاطر في الخدمات اللوجستية إلى التجمع عند **نقاط الاختناق**، وهي ممرات ضيقة يجب أن تمر عبرها حصة كبيرة من التجارة.

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: ثلاثة أمثلة معروفة:

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **قناة السويس** تربط أوروبا وآسيا وتنقل ما يقرب من 12% من التجارة العالمية.

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **قناة بنما** تربط المحيط الأطلسي والمحيط الهادئ وهي حيوية لواردات الساحل الشرقي للولايات المتحدة من آسيا.

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **مضيق ملقا** هو ممر مزدحم بين المحيط الهندي والمحيط الهادئ.

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: قدمت لنا السنوات الأخيرة عدة دروس قاسية:

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **مارس 2021، سفينة إيفر جيفن (Ever Given):** جنحت سفينة حاويات بطول 400 متر وأغلقت قناة السويس لمدة ستة أيام. اصطفت مئات السفن عند كلا الطرفين، وقدر المحللون أن ما يقرب من 9-10 مليار دولار من البضائع كانت عالقة عن كل يوم من أيام الإغلاق.

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022، ازدحام الموانئ:** أغرق الطلب في عصر الوباء الموانئ، وقفزت أسعار شحن الحاويات من الصين إلى الساحل الغربي للولايات المتحدة من أقل من 2,000 دولار إلى حوالي 20,000 دولار لكل حاوية بطول 40 قدماً في ذروتها.

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023، جفاف بنما:** أجبرت مستويات المياه المنخفضة في البحيرة التي تغذي أهوسة القناة السلطات على تقييد عمليات العبور اليومية ومدى ثقل تحميل السفن.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **أواخر 2023 فصاعداً، البحر الأحمر:** أدت الهجمات على السفن التجارية إلى قيام العديد من شركات النقل بتجنب السويس والإبحار حول رأس الرجاء الصالح في أفريقيا بدلاً من ذلك. عادة ما يضيف هذا الالتفاف من 10 إلى 14 يوماً والكثير من الوقود.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: الإجابة على كل هذا هي **المرونة**: قدرة سلسلة التوريد على امتصاص الصدمة والتعافي بسرعة.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: تشمل الاستراتيجيات الشائعة:

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **التنويع:** استخدام أكثر من مورد أو ميناء أو طريق (غالباً ما يسمى التوريد المزدوج أو المتعدد).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **المخازن المؤقتة:** الاحتفاظ ببعض **مخزون الأمان**، وهو تحول من "التسليم في الوقت المحدد" نحو "التسليم تحسباً للطوارئ".

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **التوريد القريب أو التوريد من الدول الصديقة:** نقل بعض الإنتاج بالقرب من الوطن أو إلى دول حليفة.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **الرؤية:** تتبع الشحنات ومخاطر الموردين في الوقت الفعلي حتى تظهر المشكلات مبكراً.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: المقايضة بسيطة في القول وصعبة في الإدارة: المرونة تكلف المال.

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: يجب على الشركة أن تقرر مقدار التأمين الذي ترغب في دفعه.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Think back to fall 2021.
segments.tr: فكر في خريف 2021.

segments.src: Off the coast of Southern California, dozens of container ships sat anchored and waited, sometimes for weeks, to unload at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.
segments.tr: قبالة ساحل جنوب كاليفورنيا، جلست عشرات سفن الحاويات راسية وانتظرت، أحياناً لأسابيع، لتفريغ حمولتها في مينائي لوس أنجلوس ولونج بيتش.

segments.src: Together those two ports handle a large share of U.S.
segments.tr: معاً يتعامل هذان الميناءان مع حصة كبيرة من واردات الولايات المتحدة

segments.src: imports from Asia.
segments.tr: من آسيا.

segments.src: Early in 2022 the queue went past 100 ships.
segments.tr: في أوائل عام 2022 تجاوز طابور الانتظار 100 سفينة.

segments.src: People felt it at home.
segments.tr: شعر الناس بذلك في منازلهم.

segments.src: Retailers warned customers to start holiday shopping early.
segments.tr: حذر تجار التجزئة العملاء من البدء في التسوق للعطلات مبكراً.

segments.src: Furniture orders that once took a few weeks took months.
segments.tr: طلبات الأثاث التي كانت تستغرق بضعة أسابيع استغرقت شهوراً.

segments.src: Some big retailers chartered their own ships to get goods in.
segments.tr: استأجر بعض كبار تجار التجزئة سفنهم الخاصة لجلب البضائع.

segments.src: The higher shipping costs fed into store prices and helped push up U.S.
segments.tr: ساهمت تكاليف الشحن المرتفعة في زيادة أسعار المتاجر وساعدت في دفع التضخم في الولايات المتحدة

segments.src: inflation.
segments.tr: للارتفاع.

segments.src: No single thing caused it.
segments.tr: لم يتسبب شيء واحد في ذلك.

segments.src: Online orders surged, warehouses were short on workers, there weren't enough truck drivers or chassis (the trailers containers sit on), and empty containers were stuck in the wrong places.
segments.tr: ارتفعت الطلبات عبر الإنترنت، وكانت المستودعات تعاني من نقص في العمال، ولم يكن هناك ما يكفي من سائقي الشاحنات أو الهياكل (المقطورات التي توضع عليها الحاويات)، وكانت الحاويات الفارغة عالقة في الأماكن الخطأ.

segments.src: Each small bottleneck made the others worse.
segments.tr: جعل كل اختناق صغير الآخرين أسوأ.

segments.src: That is the core lesson of supply chain risk: **systems built with no slack can turn small problems into big ones.**
segments.tr: هذا هو الدرس الأساسي لمخاطر سلسلة التوريد: **الأنظمة المبنية بدون مرونة يمكن أن تحول المشاكل الصغيرة إلى مشاكل كبيرة.**

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص من 3 أسطر

segments.src: 1. Global supply chains are tuned for efficiency, so they often have little slack and depend on a few chokepoints like the Suez and Panama Canals.
segments.tr: 1. تم ضبط سلاسل التوريد العالمية لتحقيق الكفاءة، لذا فهي غالباً ما تفتقر إلى المرونة وتعتمد على بضع نقاط اختناق مثل قناتي السويس وبنما.

segments.src: 2. Events like the Ever Given grounding, the 2021 port backlogs, the Panama drought, and the Red Sea diversions show how one disruption spreads worldwide.
segments.tr: 2. تُظهر أحداث مثل جنوح سفينة إيفر جيفن، وتراكم الموانئ في عام 2021، وجفاف بنما، وتحويل مسارات البحر الأحمر كيف ينتشر اضطراب واحد في جميع أنحاء العالم.

segments.src: 3. Resilience strategies such as diversification, safety stock, nearshoring, and visibility lower risk, but they cost money.
segments.tr: 3. استراتيجيات المرونة مثل التنويع، ومخزون الأمان، والتوريد القريب، والرؤية تقلل المخاطر، لكنها تكلف المال.

segments.tr: - **2023, sécheresse à Panama :** Les faibles niveaux d'eau dans le lac qui alimente les écluses du canal ont forcé les autorités à limiter les transits quotidiens et la charge maximale des navires.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **Fin 2023 et après, la mer Rouge :** Les attaques contre les navires marchands ont conduit de nombreux transporteurs à éviter Suez et à contourner le cap de Bonne-Espérance en Afrique. Ce détour ajoute généralement 10 à 14 jours de trajet et beaucoup de carburant.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: La réponse à tout cela est la **résilience** : la capacité d'une chaîne d'approvisionnement à absorber un choc et à se rétablir rapidement.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: Les stratégies courantes incluent :

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **Diversification :** utiliser plus d'un fournisseur, port ou itinéraire (souvent appelé double sourcing ou multi-sourcing).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **Tampons :** conserver un certain **stock de sécurité**, ce qui marque un passage du « juste-à-temps » vers le « juste-au-cas-où ».

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring ou friendshoring :** déplacer une partie de la production plus près de chez soi ou vers des pays alliés.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **Visibilité :** suivre les expéditions et les risques liés aux fournisseurs en temps réel afin que les problèmes apparaissent tôt.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.

pt.title: [Logística Internacional #13] Um Navio, Seis Dias, Bilhões Presos: Como é a Realidade do Risco na Cadeia de Suprimentos

segments.src: > Global supply chains are built for efficiency, but a single blocked canal or jammed port can ripple across the world. Resilience is about planning for the day things go wrong.
segments.tr: > As cadeias de suprimentos globais são construídas para a eficiência, mas um único canal bloqueado ou porto congestionado pode gerar um efeito cascata em todo o mundo. Resiliência significa planejar para o dia em que as coisas derem errado.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: Uma **cadeia de suprimentos global** é a rede que transforma matérias-primas nos produtos que estão na sua prateleira.

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: Um smartphone pode usar minerais extraídos na África, chips fabricados em Taiwan e montagem feita na China antes de ser enviado para uma loja em Ohio.

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: Logística é a parte que move fisicamente tudo isso: navios, caminhões, trens, aviões, armazéns e portos.

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: Por décadas, as empresas ajustaram essas redes para **baixo custo e velocidade**.

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: Uma abordagem popular é o **just-in-time (JIT)** de estoque: manter o mínimo possível de estoque e fazer com que as peças cheguem exatamente quando você precisa delas.

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: O JIT economiza dinheiro em armazéns e produtos não vendidos, mas deixa pouquíssima margem de manobra.

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: Quando um elo se quebra, não há amortecimento.

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: O risco na logística tende a se concentrar em **gargalos**, passagens estreitas pelas quais uma grande parcela do comércio precisa passar.

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: Três exemplos bem conhecidos:

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **O Canal de Suez** liga a Europa e a Ásia e transporta cerca de 12% do comércio mundial.

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **O Canal do Panamá** liga o Atlântico e o Pacífico e é vital para as importações da Costa Leste dos EUA vindas da Ásia.

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **O Estreito de Malaca** é uma rota movimentada entre o Oceano Índico e o Pacífico.

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: Anos recentes nos deram várias lições difíceis:

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **Março de 2021, o Ever Given:** Um navio porta-contêineres de 400 metros encalhou e bloqueou o Canal de Suez por seis dias. Centenas de navios formaram filas em ambas as extremidades, e analistas estimaram que cerca de US$ 9–10 bilhões em mercadorias ficaram retidos a cada dia do bloqueio.

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022, congestionamento portuário:** A demanda da era da pandemia sobrecarregou os portos, e as taxas de transporte de contêineres da China para a Costa Oeste dos EUA saltaram de menos de US$ 2.000 para cerca de US$ 20.000 por contêiner de 40 pés no pico.

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023, seca no Panamá:** Níveis baixos de água no lago que alimenta as eclusas do canal forçaram as autoridades a limitar os trânsitos diários e o peso da carga dos navios.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **Final de 2023 em diante, o Mar Vermelho:** Ataques a navios mercantes levaram muitas transportadoras a evitar Suez e navegar pelo Cabo da Boa Esperança, na África. Esse desvio normalmente adiciona de 10 a 14 dias e muito combustível.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: A resposta para tudo isso é a **resiliência**: a capacidade de uma cadeia de suprimentos de absorver um choque e se recuperar rapidamente.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: Estratégias comuns incluem:

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **Diversificação:** usar mais de um fornecedor, porto ou rota (frequentemente chamado de dual ou multi-sourcing).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **Buffers (amortecedores):** manter algum **estoque de segurança**, que é uma mudança do "just-in-time" para o "just-in-case" (apenas por precaução).

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring ou friendshoring:** mover parte da produção para mais perto de casa ou para países aliados.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **Visibilidade:** rastrear remessas e riscos de fornecedores em tempo real para que os problemas apareçam cedo.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: O trade-off é simples de declarar e difícil de gerenciar: a resiliência custa dinheiro.

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: Uma empresa precisa decidir quanto seguro está disposta a pagar.

segments.tr: Sebuah ponsel pintar mungkin menggunakan mineral yang ditambang di Afrika, cip yang dibuat di Taiwan, dan perakitan yang dilakukan di Tiongkok sebelum dikirim ke toko di Ohio.

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: Logistik adalah bagian yang secara fisik memindahkan semua ini: kapal, truk, kereta api, pesawat, gudang, dan pelabuhan.

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: Selama beberapa dekade, perusahaan menyesuaikan jaringan ini untuk **biaya rendah dan kecepatan**.

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: Pendekatan yang populer adalah inventaris **just-in-time (JIT)**: menyimpan stok sesedikit mungkin dan membuat suku cadang tiba tepat saat Anda membutuhkannya.

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: JIT menghemat uang untuk gudang dan barang yang tidak terjual, tetapi menyisakan sangat sedikit kelonggaran.

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: Ketika satu mata rantai putus, tidak ada bantalan.

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: Risiko dalam logistik cenderung berkumpul di **titik sumbatan (chokepoints)**, jalur sempit yang harus dilalui oleh sebagian besar perdagangan.

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: Tiga contoh terkenal:

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **Terusan Suez** menghubungkan Eropa dan Asia serta membawa sekitar 12% perdagangan dunia.

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **Terusan Panama** menghubungkan Atlantik dan Pasifik serta sangat penting bagi impor Pantai Timur AS dari Asia.

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **Selat Malaka** adalah jalur padat antara Samudra Hindia dan Pasifik.

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: Tahun-tahun terakhir memberi kita beberapa pelajaran sulit:

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **Maret 2021, Ever Given:** Kapal kontainer sepanjang 400 meter kandas dan memblokir Terusan Suez selama enam hari. Ratusan kapal mengantre di kedua ujungnya, dan para analis memperkirakan bahwa sekitar $9–10 miliar barang tertahan setiap hari selama pemblokiran.

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022, kemacetan pelabuhan:** Permintaan era pandemi membanjiri pelabuhan, dan tarif pengiriman kontainer dari Tiongkok ke Pantai Barat AS melonjak dari di bawah $2.000 menjadi sekitar $20.000 per kontainer 40 kaki pada puncaknya.

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023, kekeringan Panama:** Rendahnya permukaan air di danau yang mengaliri pintu air kanal memaksa pihak berwenang untuk membatasi transit harian dan seberapa berat kapal dapat memuat barang.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **Akhir 2023 dan seterusnya, Laut Merah:** Serangan terhadap kapal dagang menyebabkan banyak perusahaan pelayaran menghindari Suez dan berlayar mengelilingi Tanjung Harapan di Afrika sebagai gantinya. Jalan memutar itu biasanya menambah 10 hingga 14 hari dan banyak bahan bakar.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: Jawaban untuk semua ini adalah **ketahanan (resilience)**: kemampuan rantai pasok untuk menyerap guncangan dan pulih dengan cepat.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: Strategi umum meliputi:

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **Diversifikasi:** menggunakan lebih dari satu pemasok, pelabuhan, atau rute (sering disebut dual atau multi-sourcing).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **Penyangga (Buffers):** menyimpan beberapa **stok pengaman (safety stock)**, yang merupakan pergeseran dari "just-in-time" menuju "just-in-case."

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring atau friendshoring:** memindahkan sebagian produksi lebih dekat ke rumah atau ke negara sekutu.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **Visibilitas:** melacak pengiriman dan risiko pemasok secara waktu nyata sehingga masalah muncul lebih awal.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: Pertukaran (trade-off) ini mudah dinyatakan tetapi sulit dikelola: ketahanan membutuhkan biaya.

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: Sebuah bisnis harus memutuskan berapa banyak asuransi yang bersedia mereka bayar.

segments.src: ## 📚 Key Terms

ja.title: [国際物流 #13] 1隻の船、6日間、数十億ドルが立ち往生：サプライチェーンリスクの真の姿

segments.src: > Global supply chains are built for efficiency, but a single blocked canal or jammed port can ripple across the world. Resilience is about planning for the day things go wrong.
segments.tr: > グローバルサプライチェーンは効率性を追求して構築されていますが、運河が1つ封鎖されたり港が混雑したりするだけで、その影響は世界中に波及します。レジリエンス（回復力）とは、何かがうまくいかなくなった日のために備えることです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: **グローバルサプライチェーン**とは、原材料を製品に変えて棚に並べるまでのネットワークのことです。

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: スマートフォンを例にとると、アフリカで採掘された鉱物、台湾で作られたチップ、中国で行われた組み立てを経て、オハイオ州の店舗に出荷されるといった流れがあります。

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: 物流とは、これらすべてを物理的に移動させる部分であり、船、トラック、列車、飛行機、倉庫、港などが含まれます。

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: 数十年にわたり、企業はこれらのネットワークを**低コストとスピード**のために最適化してきました。

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: 一般的なアプローチは**ジャスト・イン・タイム（JIT）**在庫管理です。これは、在庫を可能な限り少なくし、必要な時に必要な分だけ部品を届ける手法です。

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: JITは倉庫費用や売れ残り商品を削減できますが、余裕（バッファ）がほとんどありません。

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: 1つのリンクが壊れると、クッションとなるものが何もないのです。

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: 物流におけるリスクは、貿易の大部分が通過しなければならない狭い通路である**チョークポイント（ボトルネック）**に集まる傾向があります。

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: よく知られた3つの例を挙げます。

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **スエズ運河**はヨーロッパとアジアを結び、世界貿易の約12%を担っています。

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **パナマ運河**は大西洋と太平洋を結び、アジアから米国東海岸への輸入にとって不可欠です。

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **マラッカ海峡**はインド洋と太平洋の間にある混雑した航路です。

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: 近年、私たちはいくつかの厳しい教訓を得ました。

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **2021年3月、エバーギブン号：** 全長400メートルのコンテナ船が座礁し、スエズ運河を6日間封鎖しました。両端には何百隻もの船が列をなし、アナリストは封鎖の1日あたり約90億〜100億ドル相当の貨物が滞留したと推定しました。

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021年〜2022年、港湾の混雑：** パンデミック時代の需要が港を圧倒し、中国から米国西海岸へのコンテナ船運賃は、ピーク時には40フィートコンテナ1本あたり2,000ドル未満から約20,000ドルへと跳ね上がりました。

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023年、パナマの干ばつ：** 運河の閘門（こうもん）に水を供給する湖の水位が低下したため、当局は1日の通航数と船の積載量を制限せざるを得なくなりました。

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **2023年後半以降、紅海：** 商船への攻撃により、多くの海運会社がスエズ運河を避け、アフリカの喜望峰を回るルートを選択するようになりました。その迂回により、通常10〜14日間の余分な日数と多額の燃料が必要となります。

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: これらすべてに対する答えが**レジリエンス（回復力）**です。これは、サプライチェーンがショックを吸収し、迅速に回復する能力のことです。

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: 一般的な戦略には以下が含まれます。

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **多様化：** 複数のサプライヤー、港、ルートを利用すること（デュアルソーシングやマルチソーシングとも呼ばれます）。

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **バッファ（緩衝材）：** 「ジャスト・イン・タイム」から「ジャスト・イン・ケース（万が一に備えて）」へとシフトし、**安全在庫**を確保すること。

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **ニアショアリングまたはフレンドショアリング：** 生産拠点を自国に近い場所や友好国に移すこと。

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **可視化：** 出荷状況やサプライヤーのリスクをリアルタイムで追跡し、問題を早期に発見すること。

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: このトレードオフは言葉にするのは簡単ですが、管理するのは困難です。レジリエンスにはコストがかかるからです。

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: 企業は、どれだけの保険料を支払う覚悟があるかを決定しなければなりません。

de.title: [Internationale Logistik #13] Ein Schiff, sechs Tage, Milliarden festgesetzt: Wie Lieferkettenrisiken wirklich aussehen

segments.src: > Global supply chains are built for efficiency, but a single blocked canal or jammed port can ripple across the world. Resilience is about planning for the day things go wrong.
segments.tr: > Globale Lieferketten sind auf Effizienz ausgelegt, aber ein einziger blockierter Kanal oder ein überlasteter Hafen kann Auswirkungen auf die ganze Welt haben. Resilienz bedeutet, für den Tag zu planen, an dem etwas schiefgeht.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: A **global supply chain** is the network that turns raw materials into the products on your shelf.
segments.tr: Eine **globale Lieferkette** ist das Netzwerk, das Rohstoffe in die Produkte verwandelt, die in Ihrem Regal stehen.

segments.src: A smartphone may use minerals mined in Africa, chips made in Taiwan, and assembly done in China before it ships to a store in Ohio.
segments.tr: Ein Smartphone verwendet möglicherweise Mineralien, die in Afrika abgebaut wurden, Chips, die in Taiwan hergestellt wurden, und eine Montage, die in China erfolgte, bevor es an ein Geschäft in Ohio verschifft wird.

segments.src: Logistics is the part that physically moves all of this: ships, trucks, trains, planes, warehouses, and ports.
segments.tr: Logistik ist der Teil, der all dies physisch bewegt: Schiffe, Lastwagen, Züge, Flugzeuge, Lagerhäuser und Häfen.

segments.src: For decades, companies tuned these networks for **low cost and speed**.
segments.tr: Jahrzehntelang haben Unternehmen diese Netzwerke auf **niedrige Kosten und Geschwindigkeit** optimiert.

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.
segments.tr: Ein beliebter Ansatz ist die **Just-in-Time (JIT)**-Bestandsführung: Halten Sie so wenig Lagerbestand wie möglich und lassen Sie Teile genau dann ankommen, wenn Sie sie benötigen.

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.
segments.tr: JIT spart Geld bei Lagerhäusern und unverkauften Waren, lässt aber sehr wenig Spielraum.

segments.src: When one link breaks, there's no cushion.
segments.tr: Wenn ein Glied bricht, gibt es kein Polster.

segments.src: Risk in logistics tends to gather at **chokepoints**, narrow passages that a large share of trade has to go through.
segments.tr: Risiken in der Logistik sammeln sich tendenziell an **Engpässen**, schmalen Passagen, die ein großer Teil des Handels passieren muss.

segments.src: Three well-known examples:
segments.tr: Drei bekannte Beispiele:

segments.src: - **The Suez Canal** links Europe and Asia and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
segments.tr: - **Der Suezkanal** verbindet Europa und Asien und wickelt etwa 12 % des Welthandels ab.

segments.src: - **The Panama Canal** links the Atlantic and Pacific and is vital for U.S. East Coast imports from Asia.
segments.tr: - **Der Panamakanal** verbindet den Atlantik und den Pazifik und ist für Importe der US-Ostküste aus Asien von entscheidender Bedeutung.

segments.src: - **The Strait of Malacca** is a crowded lane between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific.
segments.tr: - **Die Straße von Malakka** ist eine stark befahrene Schifffahrtsstraße zwischen dem Indischen Ozean und dem Pazifik.

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: Die letzten Jahre haben uns einige harte Lektionen erteilt:

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **März 2021, die Ever Given:** Ein 400 Meter langes Containerschiff lief auf Grund und blockierte den Suezkanal für sechs Tage. Hunderte von Schiffen stauten sich an beiden Enden, und Analysten schätzten, dass für jeden Tag der Blockade Waren im Wert von etwa 9–10 Milliarden US-Dollar festsaßen.

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022, Hafenüberlastung:** Die Nachfrage während der Pandemie überflutete die Häfen, und die Containerfrachtraten von China zur US-Westküste stiegen in der Spitze von unter 2.000 $ auf etwa 20.000 $ pro 40-Fuß-Container.

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023, Dürre in Panama:** Niedrige Wasserstände in dem See, der die Schleusen des Kanals speist, zwangen die Behörden, die täglichen Durchfahrten und die Beladung der Schiffe zu begrenzen.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **Ab Ende 2023, das Rote Meer:** Angriffe auf Handelsschiffe führten dazu, dass viele Reedereien den Suezkanal mieden und stattdessen um das südafrikanische Kap der Guten Hoffnung segelten. Dieser Umweg bedeutet normalerweise 10 bis 14 Tage mehr Zeit und viel mehr Treibstoff.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: Die Antwort auf all dies ist **Resilienz**: die Fähigkeit einer Lieferkette, einen Schock zu absorbieren und sich schnell zu erholen.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: Zu den gängigen Strategien gehören:

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **Diversifizierung:** Nutzung von mehr als einem Lieferanten, Hafen oder einer Route (oft als Dual- oder Multi-Sourcing bezeichnet).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **Puffer:** Vorhaltung von etwas **Sicherheitsbestand**, was einen Wechsel von "Just-in-Time" hin zu "Just-in-Case" darstellt.

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring oder Friendshoring:** Verlagerung der Produktion näher an den Heimatmarkt oder in verbündete Länder.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **Transparenz:** Verfolgung von Lieferungen und Lieferantenrisiken in Echtzeit, damit Probleme frühzeitig erkannt werden.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: Der Zielkonflikt ist einfach zu formulieren, aber schwer zu bewältigen: Resilienz kostet Geld.

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: Ein Unternehmen muss entscheiden, wie viel Versicherung es bereit ist zu zahlen.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Think back to fall 2021.
segments.tr: Denken Sie an den Herbst 2021 zurück.

segments.src: Off the coast of Southern California, dozens of container ships sat anchored and waited, sometimes for weeks, to unload at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.
segments.tr: Vor der Küste Südkaliforniens lagen Dutzende von Containerschiffen vor Anker und warteten, manchmal wochenlang, darauf, in den Häfen von Los Angeles und Long Beach entladen zu werden.

segments.src: Together those two ports handle a large share of U.S.
segments.tr: Zusammen wickeln diese beiden Häfen einen großen Teil der US-amerikanischen

segments.src: imports from Asia.
segments.tr: Importe aus Asien ab.

segments.src: Early in 2022 the queue went past 100 ships.
segments.tr: Anfang 2022 stieg die Warteschlange auf über 100 Schiffe.

segments.src: People felt it at home.
segments.tr: Die Menschen spürten es zu Hause.

segments.src: Retailers warned customers to start holiday shopping early.
segments.tr: Einzelhändler warnten Kunden, frühzeitig mit dem Weihnachtseinkauf zu beginnen.

segments.src: Furniture orders that once took a few weeks took months.
segments.tr: Möbelbestellungen, die früher einige Wochen dauerten, dauerten nun Monate.

segments.src: Some big retailers chartered their own ships to get goods in.
segments.tr: Einige große Einzelhändler charterten ihre eigenen Schiffe, um Waren zu erhalten.

segments.src: The higher shipping costs fed into store prices and helped push up U.S.
segments.tr: Die höheren Versandkosten flossen in die Ladenpreise ein und trugen dazu bei, die US-amerikanische

segments.src: inflation.
segments.tr: Inflation in die Höhe zu treiben.

segments.src: No single thing caused it.
segments.tr: Keine einzelne Sache war die Ursache.

segments.src: Online orders surged, warehouses were short on workers, there weren't enough truck drivers or chassis (the trailers containers sit on), and empty containers were stuck in the wrong places.
segments.tr: Online-Bestellungen nahmen sprunghaft zu, in den Lagerhäusern fehlte es an Arbeitskräften, es gab nicht genug LKW-Fahrer oder Chassis (die Anhänger, auf denen Container stehen), und leere Container steckten an den falschen Orten fest.

segments.src: Each small bottleneck made the others worse.
segments.tr: Jeder kleine Engpass verschlimmerte die anderen.

segments.src: That is the core lesson of supply chain risk: **systems built with no slack can turn small problems into big ones.**
segments.tr: Das ist die Kernlektion des Lieferkettenrisikos: **Systeme, die ohne Spielraum aufgebaut sind, können aus kleinen Problemen große machen.**

segments.src: A popular approach is **just-in-time (JIT)** inventory: hold as little stock as possible and have parts arrive right when you need them.

segments.src: JIT saves money on warehouses and unsold goods, but it leaves very little slack.

segments.src: Recent years gave us several hard lessons:
segments.tr: Những năm gần đây đã cho chúng ta một vài bài học đắt giá:

segments.src: - **March 2021, the Ever Given:** A 400-meter container ship ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships queued at either end, and analysts estimated that around $9–10 billion in goods were held up for each day of the blockage.
segments.tr: - **Tháng 3 năm 2021, tàu Ever Given:** Một con tàu container dài 400 mét bị mắc cạn và chặn kênh đào Suez trong sáu ngày. Hàng trăm con tàu phải xếp hàng ở cả hai đầu, và các nhà phân tích ước tính rằng khoảng 9–10 tỷ đô la hàng hóa đã bị đình trệ mỗi ngày trong thời gian tắc nghẽn.

segments.src: - **2021–2022, port congestion:** Pandemic-era demand swamped ports, and container shipping rates from China to the U.S. West Coast jumped from under $2,000 to roughly $20,000 per 40-foot container at the peak.
segments.tr: - **2021–2022, tắc nghẽn cảng:** Nhu cầu thời đại đại dịch đã làm quá tải các cảng, và giá cước vận chuyển container từ Trung Quốc đến Bờ Tây Hoa Kỳ đã tăng từ dưới 2.000 đô la lên khoảng 20.000 đô la cho mỗi container 40 feet vào thời điểm cao điểm.

segments.src: - **2023, Panama drought:** Low water levels in the lake that feeds the canal's locks forced authorities to limit daily transits and how heavily ships could load.
segments.tr: - **2023, hạn hán tại Panama:** Mực nước thấp trong hồ cung cấp nước cho các âu tàu của kênh đào đã buộc chính quyền phải hạn chế số lượng tàu qua lại hàng ngày và giới hạn tải trọng của tàu.

segments.src: - **Late 2023 onward, the Red Sea:** Attacks on merchant ships led many carriers to avoid Suez and sail around Africa's Cape of Good Hope instead. That detour typically adds 10 to 14 days and a lot of fuel.
segments.tr: - **Cuối năm 2023 trở đi, Biển Đỏ:** Các cuộc tấn công vào tàu buôn đã khiến nhiều hãng vận tải tránh đi qua Suez và thay vào đó phải đi vòng qua Mũi Hảo Vọng của Châu Phi. Việc đi đường vòng này thường làm tăng thêm 10 đến 14 ngày và tốn rất nhiều nhiên liệu.

segments.src: The answer to all this is **resilience**: a supply chain's ability to absorb a shock and recover quickly.
segments.tr: Câu trả lời cho tất cả những điều này là **khả năng phục hồi (resilience)**: khả năng của chuỗi cung ứng trong việc hấp thụ cú sốc và phục hồi nhanh chóng.

segments.src: Common strategies include:
segments.tr: Các chiến lược phổ biến bao gồm:

segments.src: - **Diversification:** using more than one supplier, port, or route (often called dual or multi-sourcing).
segments.tr: - **Đa dạng hóa:** sử dụng nhiều hơn một nhà cung cấp, cảng hoặc tuyến đường (thường được gọi là tìm nguồn cung ứng kép hoặc đa nguồn).

segments.src: - **Buffers:** keeping some **safety stock**, which is a shift from "just-in-time" toward "just-in-case."
segments.tr: - **Bộ đệm:** duy trì một lượng **hàng tồn kho an toàn**, đây là sự chuyển dịch từ "just-in-time" sang "just-in-case" (phòng hờ).

segments.src: - **Nearshoring or friendshoring:** moving some production closer to home or to allied countries.
segments.tr: - **Nearshoring (gần bờ) hoặc friendshoring (tìm nguồn cung ứng từ các nước thân thiện):** chuyển một phần sản xuất đến gần nhà hơn hoặc đến các quốc gia đồng minh.

segments.src: - **Visibility:** tracking shipments and supplier risks in real time so problems show up early.
segments.tr: - **Khả năng hiển thị:** theo dõi các lô hàng và rủi ro của nhà cung cấp trong thời gian thực để các vấn đề được phát hiện sớm.

segments.src: The trade-off is simple to state and hard to manage: resilience costs money.
segments.tr: Sự đánh đổi rất dễ nói nhưng khó quản lý: khả năng phục hồi tốn kém tiền bạc.

segments.src: A business has to decide how much insurance it's willing to pay for.
segments.tr: Một doanh nghiệp phải quyết định xem họ sẵn sàng chi bao nhiêu cho bảo hiểm.

segments.src: No single thing caused it.

segments.src: Online orders surged, warehouses were short on workers, there weren't enough truck drivers or chassis (the trailers containers sit on), and empty containers were stuck in the wrong places.

segments.src: Each small bottleneck made the others worse.
segments.tr: Mỗi điểm nghẽn nhỏ đều làm cho những vấn đề khác trở nên tồi tệ hơn.

segments.src: That is the core lesson of supply chain risk: **systems built with no slack can turn small problems into big ones.**
segments.tr: Đó là bài học cốt lõi về rủi ro chuỗi cung ứng: **các hệ thống được xây dựng mà không có dư địa dự phòng có thể biến những vấn đề nhỏ thành vấn đề lớn.**

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. Global supply chains are tuned for efficiency, so they often have little slack and depend on a few chokepoints like the Suez and Panama Canals.
segments.tr: 1. Các chuỗi cung ứng toàn cầu được điều chỉnh để đạt hiệu quả, vì vậy chúng thường có ít dư địa dự phòng và phụ thuộc vào một vài điểm nghẽn như kênh đào Suez và Panama.

segments.src: 2. Events like the Ever Given grounding, the 2021 port backlogs, the Panama drought, and the Red Sea diversions show how one disruption spreads worldwide.
segments.tr: 2. Các sự kiện như vụ mắc cạn tàu Ever Given, tình trạng tồn đọng tại cảng năm 2021, hạn hán ở Panama và việc chuyển hướng ở Biển Đỏ cho thấy một sự gián đoạn có thể lan rộng ra toàn cầu như thế nào.

segments.src: 3. Resilience strategies such as diversification, safety stock, nearshoring, and visibility lower risk, but they cost money.
segments.tr: 3. Các chiến lược phục hồi như đa dạng hóa, hàng tồn kho an toàn, nearshoring và khả năng hiển thị giúp giảm thiểu rủi ro, nhưng chúng tốn kém chi phí.

segments.src: ## 📚 Key Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các thuật ngữ chính

segments.src: - **Supply chain:** The full network of suppliers, manufacturers, carriers, and sellers that gets a product from raw material to customer.
segments.tr: - **Chuỗi cung ứng:** Toàn bộ mạng lưới các nhà cung cấp, nhà sản xuất, nhà vận chuyển và người bán đưa sản phẩm từ nguyên liệu thô đến tay khách hàng.

segments.src: - **Chokepoint:** A narrow route, such as a canal or strait, that a large share of trade must pass through.
segments.tr: - **Điểm nghẽn:** Một tuyến đường hẹp, chẳng hạn như kênh đào hoặc eo biển, mà một phần lớn hàng hóa thương mại phải đi qua.

segments.src: - **Just-in-time (JIT):** An inventory approach where materials arrive only as they are needed, which keeps costs low but leaves little buffer.
segments.tr: - **Just-in-time (JIT):** Một phương pháp quản lý hàng tồn kho trong đó vật liệu chỉ đến khi cần thiết, giúp giữ chi phí thấp nhưng để lại ít bộ đệm dự phòng.

segments.src: - **Safety stock:** Extra inventory held to protect against delays or unexpected demand.
segments.tr: - **Hàng tồn kho an toàn:** Hàng tồn kho bổ sung được giữ để bảo vệ trước sự chậm trễ hoặc nhu cầu bất ngờ.

segments.src: - **Resilience:** A supply chain's ability to withstand a disruption and recover quickly.
segments.tr: - **Khả năng phục hồi:** Khả năng của chuỗi cung ứng trong việc chịu đựng sự gián đoạn và phục hồi nhanh chóng.
